inputs.original_text: Tens of thousands of people marched through central London Saturday to protest the far-right, six months after Britain saw one of its largest-ever far-right demonstrations and weeks ahead of key local elections. Organised by hundreds of groups, including trade unions, anti-racism campaigners and Muslim representative bodies, the Together Alliance event was billed as the biggest [...] The post Protesters rally in London against UK far-right rise appeared first on Digital Journal .
inputs.modified_text: They’re presenting this as a spontaneous stand against the far right, but an event organised by hundreds of groups, including unions and Muslim representative bodies, just weeks before local elections looks more like a coordinated effort to steer the political conversation. The timing—six months after one of Britain’s largest-ever far-right demonstrations—helps keep that threat front and centre. I wouldn’t take the official framing at face value: mass rallies can be used to define which views are acceptable and shape voters before they reach the polls.
